text:
Diego: Quick heads-up — Orion POC running bulk embeddings hit repeated 429s on /v1/embeddings.batch during an overnight import. Demo tomorrow AM. Customer pasted the body and says they were doing 8 parallel workers with batch_size=512. Need a fast path.

Harper: Can you confirm tenant id and whether they're on a trial or paid seat? Also which model variant.

Diego: Tenant: orion-poc-9, model: embed-huge-v1, account state: trial with 50k token trial credit remaining (according to CRM). They claim they weren't near quota per their local metrics.

Mina: Trial credit exhaustion could explain it, but the 429 route is /v1/embeddings.batch which suggests per-route burst window or tenant token budget. Ask customer to send a single failed response body.

Diego: They sent this snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_limit","code":"token_budget_exhausted","retry_after_ms":2000,"route":"/v1/embeddings.batch","tenant_id":"orion-poc-9","tokens":145000}
```

Harper: Note the code token_budget_exhausted — that indicates the tenant token balance was the immediate limiter. Two paths: 1) short-term: apply a temporary credit/top-up or per-route override; 2) longer-term: advise batch/concurrency reductions.

Leah: Customer insists they had credits. CRM shows trial credit but maybe token accounting lagged or a concurrent test consumed it. They want to finish import now. Approve a short credit top-up if infra recommends.

Mina: We can do either: (A) issue a trial_topup of 200k tokens to orion-poc-9 to cover the import, expires in 2 hours; or (B) apply a per-route override tokens_per_min=280000 for 60 minutes. Top-up is lower risk for other routes. Which do you prefer?

credit-bot: [automated] Token top-up endpoint: POST /internal/billing/topup {"tenant_id":"<id>","tokens":<n>,"expires_minutes":<m>}  requires AE approval for >100k tokens.

Leah: Approving 200k top-up for 120 minutes to finish the import. I will note it in the deal log as a demo accommodation.

Mina: Applying top-up now. Top-up id: topup-20260405-17. Applied at 02:33Z.

credit-bot: [automated] Top-up topup-20260405-17 applied for tenant orion-poc-9: +200000 tokens, expires in 120 minutes.

Diego: I told the customer to resume at 02:35Z and to pause if they see more 429s. Also asked them to switch to a reduced profile: concurrency 2, batch 128 for the rest of the import.

Harper: For the POC follow-up we should add a short doc: "Trial tenants: token accounting quirks & safe import patterns" that recommends smaller batches, client-side jittered backoff, and monitoring token balance in Console. I'll draft it.

Mina: Monitoring now. No 429s in the first 12 minutes after resume. I'll keep the top-up window and report back before expiration.

Diego: Customer completed the import at 03:05Z and confirmed vectors validated. They appreciated the quick help.

credit-bot: [automated] Top-up topup-20260405-17 scheduled expiry at 04:33Z.

Mina: Top-up expired at 04:33Z; no follow-up 429 alerts. Recommending we keep the POC playbook entry and add a checklist item: check trial token balance before large imports.

Leah: Noted in CRM and will schedule a post-demo technical call to recommend permanent quota if they need sustained throughput.

Diego: Thanks team 389. Closing thread.
